what_it_does: Circuit design tools routinely split a large circuit graph into roughly equal pieces — a process called graph partitioning — so that each piece can be optimized independently. When the circuit is tweaked during design refinement, existing tools redo this splitting from scratch every time, which is wasteful. This paper introduces iG-kway, the first partitioning tool that runs on a graphics card (GPU) and is incremental: it remembers the old split and only fixes the parts of the graph that actually changed. According to the abstract, this produces results that are nearly as good as a full re-partition but much faster, which matters for the rapid iteration cycles of modern chip design.
